issue_context.title: IPv6 Compliance RFC4861: Redirected On-link: Valid (Hosts Only) [v6LC.2.3.1]
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

255

### Used distribution

Ubuntu 23

### Linux kernel version used

6.5.0-17-generic

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

x86_64

### Component

systemd-networkd

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

#### Test v6LC.2.3.1: Redirected On-link: Valid (Hosts Only)
**Purpose**: Verify that a host properly processes valid Redirect messages when redirected on-link.
**Reference**: RFC 4861, Section 4.6.1, 4.6.3, and 8.3

#### Network Configuration
```
       TR1
        |
    +---+---+
    |       |
   TN1     HUT
```

#### Procedure
| Step | Action | Expected Behavior of HUT<sup>(1)</sup> |
|--------|--------|--------|
| 1 | TR1 forwards `Echo request Src="TN1 Offlink GA"` to HUT GA<sup>(2)</sup>. | HUT sends `Echo reply` to TR1 as first hop. |
| 2 | TR1 sends `Redirect Dst="TN1 GA" Target="TN1 GA"` to HUT. | |
| 3 | TR1 forwards `Echo request Src="TN1 Offlink GA"` to HUT GA. | HUT sends `NS` for TN1's GA and `Echo reply` to TN1 on-link. |
* **(1)** - Host Under Test
* **(2)** - Global Address

The procedure is repeated with the Redirect options changing for each run.

| Run | TLLA | Redirected Packet Option |
|--------|--------|--------|
| A | No | No |
| B | No | Yes |
| C | Yes | No |
| D | Yes | Yes | 

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

`networkd` ignores the `Redirect` message.  In Step 3, `networkd` issues its `Ping reply` with first-hop being TR1.

### Steps to reproduce the problem

[v6LC_2_3_01a.zip](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/files/14366217/v6LC_2_3_01a.zip)


### Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue

_No response_

@yuwata,

I have some new information. Let me know if there is more I can do here.

The reason the tests fail is because `networkd` permanently installs a redirect route that is not being cleaned up after the test.  This causes subsequent tests to fail.

My observation is that `networkd` handles redirects differently to the `native kernel` processing. When `networkd` processes the redirect, we see the following route permanently created:

```
2001:2:0:1001:200:10ff:fe10:1180 dev enp0s9 proto ra metric 1024 mtu 1500 hoplimit 64 pref mediu
```
Q: Regarding the `proto`, it is set to `proto ra`, should this be `proto redirect`?

Compared to when the `native kernel` processes the `RA` and `Redirect`, this route is not created when the `Redirect` packet is processed.  In fact, I have not been able to observe how the kernel is maintaining its redirect route, other than to say it works, whatever it is doing. The kernel cleans up its redirect after each test.

As an encouraging side note: With `networkd`, I can get the tests to pass, as long as I manually delete the permanent redirect route before running each test.

I have attached a zip of the PCAP, containing just 3 packets that may help you investigate further. You can use the following command to send each packet one-at-a-time:

```
$ sudo tcpreplay -o -i enp0s9 tcpreplay-redirect.pcapng 
```

[tcpreplay-redirect.zip](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/files/14428576/tcpreplay-redirect.zip)

Here's a summary of the three packets:

1. RA - to setup global prefix with long lifetime
2. Redirect - for the redirect
3. RA - to clear the global prefix by setting lifetime to zero.

Here is the `networkd` debug log...

#### v6LC.2.3.7: Redirected Twice (Hosts Only)
**Purpose**: Verify that a host properly processes valid Redirect messages twice for the same destination.
**Reference**: [RFC4861 - Sections 8.3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4861#section-8.3)

#### Network Configuration
```
   TR1 TR2  TR3
    |   |   |
    +---+---+
    |       |
   TN1     HUT
```
- **TR** = Test Router
- **TN** = Test Node
- **HUT** = Host Under Test

#### Procedure
| Step | Action | Expected Behaviour of HUT |
|--------|--------|--------|
| 1 | TR1 forwards an Echo Request from TN1 to the HUT. The Source Address is the off-link global address of TN1. The Destination Address is the GA<sup>(1)</sup> of the HUT. | The HUT should respond to the Echo Request using TR1 as a first hop, as it is the only router in the HUT’s Default Router List. |
| 2 | TR1 sends `Redirect Dst="TN1 GA" Target="TR2 LLA"` to HUT. | |
| 3 | TR1 sends `Redirect Dst="TN1 GA" Target=TR2 LLA"` to HUT. | |
| 4 | TR1 forwards an Echo Request from TN1 to the HUT. The Source Address is the off-link global address of TN1. The Destination Address is the global address of the HUT. | The HUT should respond to the Echo Request using TR2 as a first hop, indicating the HUT processed the Redirect message. |
| 5 |  TR2 sends `Redirect Dst="TN1 GA" Target="TR3 LLA"` to HUT. | |
| 6 |  TR1 forwards an Echo Request from TN1 to the HUT. The Source Address is the off-link global address of TN1. The Destination Address is the global address of the HUT. | The HUT should respond to the Echo Request using TR3 as a first hop, indicating the HUT processed the Redirect message. |

* **(1)** - Global Address

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

In Step 6, the HUT responded to the Echo request using TR2, when it should have used TR3.

### Steps to reproduce the problem
[v6LC_2_3_07-Net0-20240304123454.zip](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/files/14476120/v6LC_2_3_07-Net0-20240304123454.zip)

"Redirected Header" options were added to the parser in https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/31584 (and already triggered a memory leak as far as I can remember) but they are parsed and then thrown away.
These are currently not used, may be used in a future, but not sure.

Dunno. Now that all the options are parsed unconditionally I'm not sure options like that should be there. It's true the parser is fuzzed but the fuzz target is pretty dumb in the sense that it isn't structure-aware and it can take longer than usual for it to discover even shallow issues especially given that lengths are in units of 8 octets there.
